05 / Beyond Engineering

Beyond
engineering.

Music, football, basketball, and karate. The things I return to outside the classroom and workshop.

MusicSportEveryday life
01 / Music

Music.

One of the most unforgettable milestones in my musical journey was attending the ASEAN+ Police Music Festival 2022 held in Hanoi. Immersing myself in the vibrant atmosphere and world-class performances was truly an enriching experience. A special highlight of the event was having the honor to be interviewed by Vietnam National Television (VTV), where I shared my passion for music and my perspective on this meaningful cultural exchange. It was a proud moment that continuously fuels my drive to connect with the world through music!

02 / Football

A game I grew up with.

I have loved playing football since I was a child, inspired by watching players pull off dazzling skills on the pitch. Growing up, I even dreamed of becoming a professional footballer (though that was strictly my own dream, not my parents'), so I took the sport very seriously from an early age. I played fairly regularly averaging about one match a week, and up to three or four matches a week whenever I had free time. I genuinely loved the game; whenever I had a spare moment, football was on my mind, and I would practice on my own.

My earliest achievements were winning a Silver Medal and a Bronze Medal in VietGoal tournaments organized by youth football academies. As I grew older, I continued to train and play frequently with middle school and high school friends who shared the same passion. Finally, the sweet reward I had longed for the most arrived when I recently won the championship at the HSGS Cup, our school-wide high school tournament.

03 / Basketball

Finding a new team.

Throughout elementary and middle school, I had never played basketball. However, when I entered high school, my school was renowned for the sport and had a huge community of players, which inspired me to start learning. From then on, I began practicing, watching YouTube tutorials on proper technique, and studying the rules. Fortunately, I was selected for my class basketball team and had the chance to represent my class and school in prestigious tournaments. Playing basketball allowed me to expand my social circle and learn many new things, such as how to adapt to a new environment and how to train with greater dedication. This has been a valuable lesson for me not only in basketball, but in many other areas of life as well.

04 / Karate

Learning to keep showing up.

Truthfully, when I was a kid, I didn't like practicing martial arts at all. I hated the early morning summer sun in Hanoi; at that age, I just wanted to lie in a cool, air-conditioned room without a care in the world, rolling around with my favorite Lego toys. I had no desire to step onto the training ground and face Hanoi's blazing heat. During warm-ups, every lap felt like torture, and every leg or shoulder rotation was pure misery. I would be drenched in sweat with a parched mouth and throat the more I trained, the more exhausted, hungry, and thirsty I became. The scorching heat of a Hanoi summer noon seemed to completely defeat me. When winter arrived, mornings were always the most discouraging time of day. I didn't want to leave my thick blankets at all, let alone get up and go to the park to jog and practice. Every run was a grueling struggle as the freezing wind blew against my body and down my neck. My throat would go dry, and all I wanted was to go home early, put on warm clothes, and crawl back under the covers to sleep.

However, the longer I practiced martial arts, the more I pondered what these training sessions truly gave me beyond the inherent benefits of the sport (such as physical health, self-defense, stamina, and the ability to sprint in emergencies). The answer is actually quite simple: it builds true endurance not just in muscles and physical strength, but in willpower, perseverance, and relentless consistency. Practicing martial arts also taught me discipline: keeping a regular sleep schedule, waking up early, and pushing myself to get up to train, run, and spar outdoors in harsh weather, whether freezing cold or blistering hot. Because of this, the older I get, the more silently grateful I am to my parents for having me learn martial arts.
